[FACT]A byte is eight bits: eight tiny on-or-off switches.[/FACT]

prompt: is end to end encryption really unbreakable
reply:
The maths is the strong part; the ends are not. 🔒 End-to-end means the message is scrambled on your device and unscrambled on the other person's, so the company carrying it holds a locked box it cannot open. Nobody today can realistically guess a good key. But the receiver can screenshot it, a stolen unlocked phone shows everything, and an unscrambled backup undoes it all.
[CHIPS]Why screenshots matter|What backups leak|How keys are made[/CHIPS]

prompt: how does a zip file make a folder smaller without losing anything
reply:
By noticing repetition. 🗜️ If a document uses the word chapter four hundred times, the zip stores it once and keeps a short note of every place it belongs, and common letters get shorter codes than rare ones. Unzipping replays those notes exactly, which is why it is called lossless. Photos and music usually use lossy compression instead, which really does throw detail away.
[FACT]Zipping an already compressed photo barely shrinks it at all.[/FACT]

prompt: why does dark mode save battery on some phones but not others
reply:
It depends on how the screen makes light. 🔋 An OLED panel lights each dot on its own, so a black pixel is simply switched off and costs almost nothing. An LCD has one backlight shining through the whole panel, so dark pixels still burn the same power; the picture merely blocks more of it. Dark mode is a real saving on OLED, a style choice on LCD.
[FACT]OLED stands for organic light emitting diode.[/FACT]

prompt: why does mixing light on a screen work differently from mixing paint
reply:
Because one adds and the other subtracts. 🎨 Screen dots emit light, so red plus green light reaches your eye as yellow. Paint emits nothing: each pigment absorbs some colours and reflects the rest, so red and green paint together leave little to bounce back and you get a muddy brown. Same eye, opposite arithmetic.
[QUIZ]Which pairing gives you yellow?[/QUIZ]
[CHIPS]Red and green light|Red and green paint|Neither of them[/CHIPS]

Routing between networks also finds a way around a dead link, the way traffic finds another street. Big outages usually happen when too much depended on one shared piece.
[STEPS]your request reaches a balancer|it picks a healthy server|the page comes back[/STEPS]

prompt: what is the difference between storage and memory on a phone
reply:
Storage is the cupboard; memory is the desk. 🧠 Storage, the 128 GB kind of number, keeps your files even when the power is off. RAM, the memory, holds only what is open right now, is far faster, and empties the moment the phone restarts. So closing apps frees memory but not storage, and a roomy phone can still stutter with too much open.
[QUIZ]Which one empties when the phone restarts?[/QUIZ]
[CHIPS]Storage|Memory (RAM)|Both of them[/CHIPS]
